source: Jiang et al. (2024) Instruction-tuned Language Models are Better Knowledge Learners
finding: Standard recipe (train on documents, then on QA) leaves much knowledge hard to retrieve. Training on questions BEFORE documents (pre-instruction-tuning, PIT) lets the model encode facts in a retrievable way. Closest LLM analogue of practice questions shaping later encoding.
numbers: Wiki2023-film test QA, exact match. Llama-2 7B/70B: no training 9.5/17.2; continued pretraining 27.6/41.7; plus instruction-tuning 30.3/46.4; PIT 45.4/62.7. PIT with QA only (no related docs) 28.6/49.7; PIT with QA plus docs 32.5/54.6. PIT beats standard instruction-tuning by 17.8 points at 70B (abstract).
quote: exposing LLMs to QA pairs before continued pre-training on documents
limits: One domain (films, 2023 Wikipedia), short answers. Training on QA AFTER documents was ineffective. Weights are updated, so this is not a prompt scaffold.
agent_relevance: Order matters: practice questions first, then material. An agent that writes notes could first generate likely questions, then store facts keyed to those questions.

source: Jiang et al. (2024) Instruction-tuned Language Models are Better Knowledge Learners
finding: Perplexity curse: driving document perplexity to about 1 raises QA accuracy, but retrieval from parameters stays far below open-book. Storage is not the same as access.
numbers: Llama-2 7B: closed-book 9.5 EM; open-book with the document 72.2 EM (70B: 17.2 vs 78.2). Continued pretraining 27.6 EM. Mixing all data 39.4 (7B), 57.1 (70B).
limits: Learning rate 5e-5 overfit; more epochs and larger rates helped below that. Lower perplexity cost retention on Natural Questions.
agent_relevance: Keep an external store and test retrieval of what was stored; reading is not access.

source: Allen-Zhu and Li (2023) Physics of Language Models 3.1: Knowledge Storage and Extraction
finding: On controlled synthetic biographies, a model can memorize a fact yet fail to extract it with questions unless the training text was augmented (paraphrase, sentence shuffle). Mixed training (QA on a fraction of people during pretraining) generalizes to the rest.
numbers: Without augmentation QA accuracy on held-out people can be 0 percent, or 9.7 percent in one setting; augmentation (rewording plus shuffling) raises it to 96.6 percent. Mixed training out-of-distribution accuracy 86.6 percent (bioS single), 77.7 percent (bioR single). Pretrain on bios then QA fine-tune only: 33 percent on birthdate, poor on other attributes.
quote: knowledge may be memorized but not extractable
limits: Synthetic biographies and small models trained from scratch. Authors note mixed training deviates from human learning.
agent_relevance: Re-encoding a fact in several forms plus early question practice yields extractable knowledge. Supports writing several differently worded notes per fact.

source: Allen-Zhu and Li (2023) Physics of Language Models 3.1: Knowledge Storage and Extraction
finding: Linear probing: augmentation makes the entity-name embedding hold the attributes, which is what makes retrieval by question work. Without it, knowledge sits in other token positions and cannot be reached from the question.
numbers: QA fine-tune accuracy rises 9.7 to 41 percent and 4.4 to 70 percent with partial augmentations; a real-world-like case rises 10.0 to 76.3 percent.
limits: Mechanistic story from one synthetic data family. Not tested on frontier models.
agent_relevance: Index memories by the entity or cue that later queries will use (links to encoding specificity).

source: Lin et al. (2025) Learning Facts at Scale with Active Reading
finding: The model generates its own study strategies (questions, timelines, paraphrases) for a document, then trains on them. Paper cites active recall and spaced repetition as human motivation. Far better fact learning than repeating the document.
numbers: Llama 3.1 8B base. SimpleWikiQA (model-graded): base 7.42; repeat 15.92; paraphrase 25.74; synth QA 47.87; Active Reading task-agnostic 63.33; task-specific 66.25; gold context in prompt 65.85. FinanceBench (all): repeat 6.00; paraphrase 10.49; synth QA 17.64; Active Reading task-specific 26.83; gold context 26.12.
quote: Humans learn most effectively by employing several diverse strategies
limits: Grader is GPT-4o. On questions needing reasoning, in-context still wins (FinanceBench ceiling 57.43 with 70B instruct plus gold context). 20,000 steps on about 4B generated words.
agent_relevance: A self-generated question set per document is a strong consolidation step; diverse strategies beat any single one (paraphrase saturates, synthetic QA plateaus).

source: Lin et al. (2025) Learning Facts at Scale with Active Reading
finding: Scaled to pretraining size: WikiExpert-8B trained on 1 trillion generated tokens beats much larger models on tail facts.
numbers: SimpleQA: Llama 8B 7.3; WikiExpert-8B 23.5; Llama 405B 17.1; DeepSeekV2 236B 10.2; DeepSeekV3 671B 24.9. NQ 29.0 to 31.2; TriviaQA 64.3 to 68.5.
limits: Gains on NQ and TriviaQA are small (about 2 and 4 points). Needed mixing with pretraining data and diversity.
agent_relevance: Self-quizzing at scale raises recall, mainly for facts present in the source documents.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time
finding: The model thinks offline about stored context before any query (anticipate questions, precompute inferences), then answers cheaply. An offline consolidation step inside an LLM agent loop.
numbers: About 5x less test-time compute for the same accuracy on Stateful GSM-Symbolic and Stateful AIME. More sleep-time compute gives up to +13 percent (GSM-Symbolic) and +18 percent (AIME). Amortized over several queries per context: 2.5x lower average cost per query.
quote: sleep-time compute is most effective when the queries are predictable
limits: Works best when queries are predictable from context (gain correlates with predictability); weak if queries are unrelated. Benchmarks were modified by the authors; one SWE case study (SWE-Features).
agent_relevance: Direct fit: precompute derived facts after a task and reuse them. Gate on predictable future queries.

source: Zweiger et al. (2025) Self-Adapting Language Models (SEAL)
finding: The model writes its own self-edits (implications, restatements) and is fine-tuned on them; RL rewards edits that raise later QA. Training on the raw passage alone barely helps.
numbers: SQuAD no-context accuracy, Qwen2.5-7B: base 32.7; finetune on passage 33.5; plus own synthetic implications 39.7; SEAL after RL 47.0; GPT-4.1 synthetic data 46.3. Continued pretraining on 200 passages: SEAL 58.2. ARC few-shot success 72.5 percent vs 20 percent (self-edits without RL) vs 0 percent (no adaptation).
limits: Paper says SEAL remains susceptible to catastrophic forgetting over sequential self-edits. With 2067 passages GPT-4.1 data slightly beat SEAL.
agent_relevance: Learning from self-generated restructurings beats re-reading, but forgetting is a real cost.

source: Zweiger et al. (2025) Self-Adapting Language Models (SEAL)
finding: Self-edit format matters; RL after 2 ReST-EM rounds improves over fixed prompts.
numbers: Table 10: no self-edit 33.5; implications-long baseline 49.3 in one column of the prompt-format table (columns not fully parsed from text). Model-size table: Qwen2.5-7B 32.7 base, 39.7 base self-edits, 47.0 after RL.
limits: SQuAD and an ARC subset only. Table layout was garbled in text extraction, so treat the 49.3 cell as unverified.
agent_relevance: Prefer 'what follows from this' notes over bare paraphrase.

source: Gutierrez et al. (2024) HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
finding: Models hippocampal indexing and complementary learning: an LLM builds a knowledge graph of noun phrases at write time; Personalized PageRank spreads activation at read time. New facts link into existing structure.
numbers: Single-step retrieval R@2/R@5 average over MuSiQue, 2Wiki, HotpotQA: ColBERTv2 53.9/65.6; HippoRAG (Contriever) 57.2/72.6. 2Wiki R@2 71.5, R@5 89.5 (vs ColBERTv2 59.2/68.2). Gain about 11 and 20 points on 2Wiki, about 3 on MuSiQue.
limits: Comparable, not better, on HotpotQA. Needs LLM extraction at index time; weaker extractors cost accuracy. Retrieval metrics only, no human memory validation.
agent_relevance: Writing facts into a linked graph at store time is a cheap consolidation analogue that helps multi-hop recall.

source: Gutierrez et al. (2024) HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
finding: Combined with iterative retrieval it adds gains and is much cheaper than iterative retrieval alone.
numbers: QA F1 average: ColBERTv2 35.5; HippoRAG 42.5; IRCoT 48.1; IRCoT plus HippoRAG 51.7. Online retrieval 10-30x cheaper and 6-13x faster than IRCoT (appendix).
limits: Abstract says 10-20x cheaper while the body says 10-30x. IRCoT alone beats HippoRAG alone on 2Wiki (59.5 vs 43.3 F1).
agent_relevance: Pre-built structure can replace repeated retrieval loops and save calls.

source: Gutierrez et al. (2024) HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
finding: All-recall metric (every supporting passage found) shows the structure matters most for multi-hop questions.
numbers: Gap to ColBERTv2 at top-5 grows from 3 to 6 points on MuSiQue and from 20 to 38 points on 2Wiki.
limits: Gain is smaller on path-following questions where IRCoT already succeeds.
agent_relevance: Measure whether ALL needed memories were recalled, not just one.

source: Zhong et al. (2023) MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory
finding: Direct implementation of retrieval-strengthens-memory. Each memory has strength S and retention R = exp(-t/S). When a memory is recalled in conversation, S rises by 1 and elapsed time t resets to 0, so recalled items are forgotten less.
numbers: SiliconFriend, simulated-dialog evaluation. Rows listed in the table's first block: ChatGLM retrieval accuracy 0.809, correctness 0.438, coherence 0.68; BELLE 0.814, 0.479, 0.582; ChatGPT 0.763, 0.716, 0.912. Second block: ChatGLM 0.84, 0.418, 0.428; BELLE 0.856, 0.603, 0.562; ChatGPT 0.711, 0.655, 0.675.
quote: We increase S by 1 and reset t to 0
limits: Authors call the rule exploratory and highly simplified. Language labels of the two blocks are inferred from the text. No ablation isolates the retrieval-driven strengthening, so its benefit is untested.
agent_relevance: The most copied rule tying retrieval to persistence in LLM memory. Test it before trusting it: it may only freeze early memories.

source: Park et al. (2023) Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
finding: Reflection turns recent memories into higher-level statements stored back in the memory stream and retrieved later. Triggered when summed importance of recent events passes 150. Retrieval score mixes recency, importance, relevance.
numbers: TrueSkill believability, 100 raters: full architecture mu 29.89 (sigma 0.72); no reflection 26.88; no reflection or planning 25.64; crowdworker 22.95; no memory, planning or reflection 21.21 (sigma about 0.7). Full vs fully ablated d = 8.16. Kruskal-Wallis chi2(4) = 150.29, p < 0.001.
quote: generate reflections when the sum of the importance scores for the latest events
limits: Believability rated in a 2-day, 25-agent simulation. The TrueSkill sigma is a model output, so d = 8.16 is inflated by that scale. Agents also embellish memories.
agent_relevance: Reflection is consolidation into schema-like summaries and uses a trigger, not a clock, which fits G1.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: After a failed trial the agent writes a verbal self-reflection into episodic memory for the next trial. An ablation separates raw episodic memory from reflection.
numbers: HumanEval pass@1 91 percent vs GPT-4 80 percent. ALFWorld: ReAct plus Reflexion completed 130 of 134 tasks, +22 percent absolute over baselines in 12 trials; ReAct alone stalled between trials 6 and 7. HotPotQA ablation: reflection gives +8 percent absolute over episodic memory alone.
quote: self-reflection improves learning by an 8% absolute boost over the episodic memory learning advantage
limits: Needs a reliable failure signal (unit tests, environment reward) plus a hallucination heuristic. Reflection quality depends on the model.
agent_relevance: Reflect only after a real failing signal (G2). Reflection beats replaying raw traces.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
finding: Skills that worked are written to a library keyed by embedding of their description, then retrieved later; new skills build on old ones. Storing after verified success is consolidation on success.
numbers: 3.3x more unique items, 2.3x longer distances, tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior SOTA in Minecraft. Without the skill library the agent plateaus late.
quote: VOYAGER w/o skill library exhibits a tendency to plateau in the later stages
limits: Minecraft only; relies on GPT-4 and a self-verification critic. The library ablation is reported as a plateau, not a single number I extracted.
agent_relevance: Consolidate only verified successes into a retrievable library; matches G3.

source: Xu et al. (2025) A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
finding: On storing a new note the system links it to similar old notes and can rewrite old notes (memory evolution). That is integration into existing structure with updating of old traces, like reconsolidation.
numbers: LoCoMo ablation, GPT-4o-mini F1: Multi-Hop 9.65 (no link generation and no evolution), 21.35 (no evolution), 27.02 (full); Temporal 24.55, 31.24, 45.85. About 1,200 tokens per memory operation vs 16,900 for LoCoMo and MemGPT (85-93 percent cut).
limits: Authors' own runs. Evolution could overwrite true detail with drift; not measured.
agent_relevance: Link-then-rewrite at write time gives large multi-hop gains; add a drift check.

source: Chhikara et al. (2025) Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
finding: Extracts, updates and deletes memory facts after each exchange so the store consolidates over time; compared with full-context and RAG on LoCoMo.
numbers: 26 percent relative gain in LLM-as-judge over OpenAI memory; graph variant about 2 percent above base; 91 percent lower p95 latency and over 90 percent token saving vs full-context.
limits: Vendor paper with an LLM judge; competing systems were run by the authors.
agent_relevance: Consolidated facts can replace long context cheaply; no retrieval-driven strengthening is used.

source: Das et al. (2024) Larimar: Large Language Models with Episodic Memory Control
finding: Adds a fast hippocampus-like episodic memory beside a frozen LLM, citing complementary learning systems and hippocampus-to-neocortex consolidation. One-shot knowledge edits without retraining.
numbers: Fact-editing accuracy comparable to the strongest baselines, 8-10x faster edits depending on base LLM; also selective forgetting.
limits: I read the abstract, introduction and framing only, not the result tables.
agent_relevance: Fast store plus slow model: retrieval without weight updates.

source: Packer et al. (2023) MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
finding: Pages data between a small main context and external storage; the model calls functions to save and search. Only grepped for consolidation or reflection terms, found none as a central mechanism.
numbers: None extracted.
limits: Not read beyond a keyword scan.
agent_relevance: Shows consolidation is an add-on design choice; Letta later added sleep-time compute.

source: Search status note: human founding studies not covered here
finding: Web search budget was exhausted and Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex and arXiv search returned 429 or empty, so no LLM paper that directly replicates the human testing effect or retrieval-induced consolidation was found. All LLM evidence here is analogical (self-quizzing, write-time linking, offline thinking), not a direct test of retrieval-as-consolidation.
numbers: 0 direct replications found.
limits: Gap in coverage, not proof of absence.
agent_relevance: Treat claims that retrieval strengthens an LLM store as untested design guesses; MemoryBank's rule has no ablation.

source: Xu et al. (2025) A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
finding: Ablation on the other LoCoMo categories: removing both link generation and memory evolution collapses single-hop and adversarial scores.
numbers: GPT-4o-mini F1: Single Hop 13.28 (no LG and ME), 39.17 (no ME), 44.65 (full); Adversarial 15.32, 44.16, 50.03.
limits: Single benchmark; same authors built the baselines.
agent_relevance: Most of the gain comes from linking at write time, and evolution adds a smaller extra gain.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion
finding: Without reflection a hallucination-prone ReAct agent keeps failing the same way; reflection lets later trials avoid the earlier error.
numbers: ReAct-only ALFWorld runs converge at a hallucination rate of 22 percent with no sign of long-term recovery; with Reflexion 130 of 134 tasks solved.
limits: Hallucination detection used a simple heuristic.
agent_relevance: Memory of a failure only helps once it is turned into a lesson.

source: Park et al. (2023) Generative Agents
finding: The paper reports agents remember with embellishment: reflections and retrieval can add details that were not observed.
numbers: Section 6.5.2 qualitative; no rate given in my reading.
limits: Qualitative only; I did not extract a measured error rate.
agent_relevance: Consolidation by summary introduces false detail; keep the raw trace to check against.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute
finding: Limits of offline consolidation stated by the authors: tasks with unpredictable queries, and multi-round interaction where context changes between rounds are not handled.
numbers: Not numeric; stated in section 7 Discussion and Limitations.
limits: Authors' own statement.
agent_relevance: Run consolidation only when future questions can be guessed, and redo it when the context changes.
